title: int8 smoothscale rendezvous: kernel handoff + KV-aware scheduler for continuous batching
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Improved INT8 kernel handoff for streaming workloads: reduced tail latency by ~18% and lowered per-token compute by ~12% for common sequence-length distributions. Includes scheduler improvements that coordinate KV cache affinity with continuous batching windows.
body: Motivation: Streaming inference workloads showed uneven latency tails when mixing quantized kernels and fp32 fallbacks during dynamic batching. This PR implements a lightweight 'rendezvous' handoff between INT8-optimized kernels and fallback execution paths, combined with a KV-aware scheduler that aligns continuous-batching windows with KV cache affinity so that prefetched KV state is reused more deterministically. Summary of changes: 1) new kernel handoff protocol in the runtime that exposes a minimal ABI for passing KV affinity metadata, 2) scheduler additions to track per-request KV fingerprints and form rendezvous groups that prefer homogenous quantization paths, 3) minor changes to the kernel loader to surface throughput/latency profiles for runtime routing decisions, 4) e2e perf tests and a calibration script that collects sequence length and KV hit statistics. Checklist: - [x] Design doc and microbenchmark results included - [x] Unit tests for handoff logic - [x] Integration perf harness and recording - [x] CI passing on main matrix - [x] Backcompat: handoff is opt-in behind runtime flag for now Implementation notes: The handoff protocol is intentionally minimal: it passes a tokenized KV fingerprint string, a preferred quantization tag (int8/fp8/fp32), and a micro-decision hint (prefer_low_latency / prefer_throughput). Runtime uses this to deterministically route a request through the same kernel group for the duration of a batch or to fall back if capacity isn't available. The KV-aware scheduler keeps a small LRU of recent KV fingerprints per worker and biases rendezvous group formation to avoid mixing high-mismatch requests into the same continuous-batch, which previously caused repeated KV reloads and higher latency variance. Performance summary: On our internal LAMBDA-small benchmark with mixed sequence lengths, steady-state throughput is flat but p95 latency improves by 18% and token compute drops by ~12% on average when the feature flag is enabled. For large-sequence tails the scheduler reduces KV reloads by ~30%. Commits: single squash for merge. See commits list for atomic changes. High-level changed files: runtime/kernel_handoff.cpp runtime/kernel_handoff.h runtime/kernel_interface_v2.h scheduler/kv_rendezvous_scheduler.cpp scheduler/kv_affinity.h scheduler/continuous_batcher.cpp runtime/loader/kernel_loader.cpp tests/perf/bench_int8_streaming.py tests/unit/test_kernel_handoff.py docs/rfc/int8-smoothscale-rendezvous.md build/CMakeLists.txt Why this is safe: The new handoff is behind a runtime flag and defaults to disabled. Kernel ABI changes are additive; older kernels are untouched. The scheduler is additive and conservative: it only biases group formation, never rejects requests. Rollout plan: enable flag for canary pool, run perf harness for 48h, gradually expand to 50% of serving capacity, monitor p95/p99 and KV miss rates. Related PRs and background: This builds on telemetry collected by ENG-1423 and the kernel profiling work in ENG-1487. It is complementary to other quantization-path work but focuses on runtime routing and KV cache alignment rather than new quant kernels.

review_comments: Diego Alvarez: The rendezvous idea looks promising. Can we ensure the fingerprint is compact and won't add overhead to hot-paths? Please add microbenchmarks for encoding/decoding the fingerprint.
Maya Chen: Added compact varint-based encoding; microbenchmarks are in tests/perf/bench_int8_streaming.py with allocation numbers. Encoding cost is <0.5% of token compute on our microbench.
Priya Raman: Scheduler biasing needs to be cautious about overheavy skew in multi-tenant pools. Suggest a tunable threshold and fallthrough to default policy.
Maya Chen: Added tunable thresholds and documented safe defaults in the RFC. Scheduler falls back to round-robin if a rendezvous would starve capacity.
Samir Patel: Did you validate fallback behavior when an INT8 kernel is busy but fp32 is free? Need predictable degradation path.
Maya Chen: Yes, runtime will prefer same-path rendezvous for the batch build but will fall back to the fastest available compatible kernel; tests added to validate this path.
Priya Raman: CI perf flaky on one run. Please re-run perf job before merge.
Maya Chen: Re-ran perf suite; results stable. CI now green.
Diego Alvarez: Approving with two nits in comments (inline).
notes: Opt-in runtime flag: RUNTIME_INT8_RENDEZVOUS=false by default. Feature gated in release notes.
observability_changes: Added metrics: sched.rendezvous_groups_created sched.kv_reuse_rate runtime.handoff_hits runtime.handoff_misses. Exposed as tags for per-model dashboards.
postmerge_actions: Rollout to canary pool, run 48h perf check, monitor metrics, if stable schedule broader rollout with ops runbook.
testing: Unit tests exercise encoding/decoding, scheduler bias thresholds, and fallback. Perf harness covers mixed-length streaming workload and records KV reload counts and latency histograms. Calibration script included to generate fingerprints and measure hit distributions.
security_review: No new credential or network surface; handoff token is an internal opaque identifier, validated and sanitized. Security review completed by security team.
changelog_entry: Improve INT8 streaming latency via kernel handoff and KV-aware rendezvous scheduler (opt-in runtime flag).
